clue.text: Confound attack, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word for an attack is to be taken as it is spoken

parts.note: a throe is a sudden attack or spasm of pain

explanation.surface: Someone is baffled by an assault they only heard about.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewilder or disconcert someone is to put them off balance, a sense of confound.

clue.text: Turned up to make furrow over-extended

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the letters for making a furrow are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to dig a rut is to make a furrow in the ground

explanation.surface: A ploughman's furrow is turned up to become overlong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' looks like ploughing language but is the reversal signal: DIG RUT read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Swollen or bloated, as prose padded beyond its natural size; a synonym in the sense of inflated.

clue.text: Grub, mostly baby turnip?

indicators.note: mostly means the word for a baby turnip loses its final letter

parts.note: a rootlet is a small root, which a baby turnip might fairly be called

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a small turnip counts as food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last T of ROOTLET. Grub here is a verb: to dig or poke about.
explanation.definitionFit: To grub is to rummage or dig about in the soil, as a pig does with its snout; a synonym.

clue.text: Criminal rode?

parts.note: the clue word rode is the letters D, O, E, R put in the wrong order, so it is a scrambled 'doer'

explanation.surface: A one-word question: was riding somehow a crime?
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as instructions: wrong (an anagram signal) applied to DOER produces the clue's 'rode'.
explanation.definitionFit: An offender who breaks the law is a lawbreaker or criminal; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Blessed end to prayer, first to last in Irish town

parts.note: bally is a mild British euphemism for bloody, just as blessed is used as a mild oath

indicators.note: first to last tells us to move the opening letter of the prayer's ending to the back

parts.note: amen is the word said at the end of a prayer

explanation.surface: A worshipper reaches the final word of a prayer in a town in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to last' moves the A of AMEN to the end, giving MENA. Bally is dated British slang for 'blessed' or 'damned'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballymena is a town in County Antrim, Northern Ireland; an example of an Irish town.

clue.text: Some academic is about to take up language

indicators.note: in a down entry, to take up means the hidden letters are read upwards
some says only part of the run of words 'academic is about' is used

explanation.surface: A scholar is about to begin studying a foreign tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks CISAB from academiC IS ABout, and 'to take up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: BASIC is an early programming language, so a computer language rather than a spoken one.

clue.text: One flaps quietly till towel is disentangled

indicators.note: disentangled suggests the letters of 'till towel' are teased out into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone shakes out a towel quietly until it comes untangled.
explanation.walkthrough: The flapping towel misleads: 'One flaps quietly' is the bird, and 'disentangled' rearranges TILL TOWEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Owls fly almost silently, and this small European owl is one bird whose wings beat noiselessly.

clue.text: A bit of conviviality entailed gossip

indicators.note: a bit of says only a portion of the words 'conviviality entailed' is wanted

explanation.surface: A sociable evening involved a little chatter about others.
explanation.definitionFit: A yenta is a Yiddish term for a busybody or meddler, so a person who gossips.

clue.text: Threat for lost hiker — getting shot?

definitions.meaning: a walker stranded on a hill risks dying from the cold and wind of being unsheltered
in photography, each frame taken on film is one of these, so getting a shot means making one

explanation.surface: A lost hiker faces danger, possibly being shot.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both being unprotected from the elements and a single frame of camera film.

clue.text: Group with skill covering chaos up

indicators.note: covering means the skilful word wraps round the other piece

parts.note: ably means with skill

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word for chaos is read upwards

parts.note: a mess is a state of chaos

explanation.surface: A capable team brings order to disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with skill' reads like a description of the group, but it supplies the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering of people met together, such as a school assembly, is a group; a synonym.

clue.text: Very lively SA city, as viewed by NA?

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a South American city
to us, from the point of view of North Americans

explanation.surface: A South American city seems exciting to North American visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: SA and NA are South and North America; 'as viewed by' gives the phrase TO US.
explanation.definitionFit: Unruly, boisterous and full of high spirits, as a riotous party; a synonym for very lively.

clue.text: Time opponents seized leadership of Paris, so much the worse for Hollande

definitions.text: so much the worse for Hollande

indicators.note: seized means the opponents' word grips the next letter inside it

parts.note: antis are people who are against something

indicators.note: leadership of means just the first letter of Paris is used

explanation.surface: Rivals take control of Paris, which is bad luck for a French president.
explanation.walkthrough: François Hollande was French president, so the definition asks for a French phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Tant pis is French for too bad, or never mind, an idiom of resigned regret.

clue.text: Gallon I consumed in pub after one left — not sensible

indicators.note: after places the pub following the two letters for one and left

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: consumed in means the gallon and I go inside the pub

parts.note: a local is a British pub near one's home

explanation.surface: Drinking a gallon in the pub after a friend has gone is foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumed in' puts G and I inside LOCAL, a British word for one's neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking logic or sound reasoning, an idea that makes no sense; a synonym.

clue.text: Cut in business money here

indicators.note: cut means the word for business is shortened by its last letter

parts.note: ado is fuss or business, as in much ado
a sum is an amount of money

explanation.surface: Someone discusses cuts to company funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' trims ADO to AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Adsum is Latin for I am present, the reply at a roll call, so the same as saying 'here'.

clue.text: Job to accomplish court examination, requiring much education

parts.note: a post is a job
to do something is to accomplish it
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A job applicant has to pass a court-run test needing lots of schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: Postdoctoral research comes after a PhD, so it needs a great deal of prior education.

clue.text: Noted drink — brew of 'ot water?

indicators.note: brew suggests the words 'of 'ot water' are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A famous drink is made from hot water, said in Cockney fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' means set to musical notes: the drink is a song title.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known popular song from the musical No, No, Nanette, so a drink with music attached.

clue.text: Russian noblewomen, one with various servants about

indicators.note: various suggests the letters of 'servants' and the A are mixed into a new order

parts.note: a means one

explanation.surface: Russian ladies, each attended by several servants.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarevna was the daughter of a Russian tsar, so these women were Russian royalty.

clue.text: Stress success for Spooner should be kept secret

indicators.note: for Spooner means the opening letters of the two words are swapped

parts.note: to rack is to stress or strain severely
a boom is a period of success

explanation.surface: A tense triumph that ought to be hushed up.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the R and B of RACK BOOM gives BACK ROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Backroom dealings are done in private, behind the scenes, so kept secret; an adjectival sense.

clue.text: Rude apprentice seen around church

indicators.note: around means the word for apprentice goes round the church letters

parts.note: to indent is to bind someone as an apprentice by indenture
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A young trainee behaves impolitely while visiting a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apprentice' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecent means improper or offensive, as rude jokes are; a synonym in that sense.

clue.text: One beginning to bother all on road when travelling round motorway?

definitions.text: One beginning to bother all on road when travelling round motorway?

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of bother is used
round means the scrambled letters go round the motorway letter
travelling suggests the letters of 'all on road' are moved around

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in M1

explanation.surface: An outsize vehicle slows everyone down as it inches round a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges ALL ON ROAD into NORALLOAD, and 'round' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversized vehicle shipment needing escort, which troubles all other drivers on its route.

clue.text: Irish writer quit, replacing last letter with a Greek character

indicators.note: replacing last letter with means the final letter is swapped for what follows

parts.note: left is the past tense of leave, so quit
nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: An Irish author gives up writing, swapping a letter for one from Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Sheridan Le Fanu was a nineteenth-century Dublin author of gothic ghost stories.

clue.text: The actual thing is a fairy clutching top of tree

indicators.note: clutching means the outer pieces hold the next letter inside
top of means just the first letter of tree

parts.note: an elf is a fairy

explanation.surface: A real fairy grips the top of a Christmas tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Used for emphasis, the pronoun means the very thing and no other; an idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Joints and spotted dick finally returned

indicators.note: returned means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: spotted means seen

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of dick is used

explanation.surface: Joints of meat and a spotted dick pudding come back to the table.
explanation.walkthrough: Spotted dick is a British steamed suet pudding with currants, but 'spotted' is just SEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The hinge joints in the middle of the legs; examples of joints.

clue.text: Damp area took to water power

parts.note: swam means took to the water

explanation.surface: A wet patch where someone swam using strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterlogged marshy ground, a bog or marsh; a damp area.

clue.text: English king limited by clear strain?

indicators.note: limited by means the English king is enclosed by the clear word

parts.note: overt means clear and open
rex is Latin for king

explanation.surface: An English monarch is constrained by an obvious tension.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that strain is a verb, to push too hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To push oneself beyond one's limits is to strain too much; a synonym with excess implied.

clue.text: Overhanging items — i.e. line removed from top of pages

indicators.note: removed from top of means the letter is taken off the front of the word

parts.note: leaves are pages of a book

explanation.surface: Some overhanging items, such as a line cut from the head of a page.
explanation.definitionFit: The edges of a roof that jut out beyond the walls; overhanging parts of a building.

clue.text: About to carve ham

indicators.note: about suggests the letters of 'to carve' are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is about to carve a joint of ham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ham' looks like the meat but is the verb: to perform with exaggeration.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to perform in an exaggerated, theatrical way, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Superior contest involving two different names

indicators.note: involving means the contest word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: to vie is to contest or compete
N is the abbreviation for name, and a tag is another word for a name

explanation.surface: A top-class competition between two named rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: Vintage means of high quality or classic, as a vintage performance; a synonym.

clue.text: Figures of speech — the writer's touch hack fails to complete

parts.note: the writer is the setter, who calls themselves me
to tap is to touch lightly

indicators.note: fails to complete means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a hack is a horse for hire or riding

explanation.surface: A writer's journalism lacks the finishing touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hack' suggests a journalist but is a riding horse; 'fails to complete' trims HORSE to HORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative expressions comparing one thing to another; examples of figures of speech.

clue.text: Boss finally dismissed following unspecified things

indicators.note: finally dismissed means the final letter is removed

parts.note: a boss is a raised knob or stud
ff is the abbreviation for following pages

explanation.surface: A manager is eventually sacked after various matters arise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like a manager but is a stud or knob.
explanation.definitionFit: General vague material or matter, as in 'all that stuff'; an informal synonym.
